title: How Far Back the Relief Window Reaches on a Personal Checking Account
content:
**Clause.** The length of the relief window on a Personal Checking account moves with the overdraft charges standing on it, with the owner's premier money market balance held under Savings & Money Market Accounts and with card payments under Personal Credit Cards.

1. Where at least 3 overdraft charges stand on the account **and** the owner's premier money market balance reaches the protection source minimum of 5000.00, the relief window is a long relief window of 6 calendar months.
2. Where the case above does not apply **and** either at least 2 overdraft charges stand **or** the owner has made at least 6 card payments in the last twelve months, it is a middle relief window of 3 calendar months.
3. Where neither case applies, neither of those lengths is used.

The window runs back from the day the matter is handled, and the overdraft charges posted inside it are the ones the window admits.

**Worked windows on hypothetical inputs.** An account carries overdraft charges posted 1, 2, 4 and 7 calendar months ago.

| Owner's position | Relief window | Overdraft charges inside it |
|---|---|---|
| 4 overdraft charges standing, premier money market balance of 9000.00 | 6 calendar months | The charges posted 1, 2 and 4 months ago |
| 4 overdraft charges standing, premier money market balance of 300.00 | 3 calendar months | The charges posted 1 and 2 months ago |
| 1 overdraft charge standing, 7 card payments in the last twelve months | 3 calendar months | The charges posted 1 and 2 months ago |
| 1 overdraft charge standing, 2 card payments | Neither length is used |  |

The first case requires both of its limbs; the second is met by either limb alone. Equality satisfies each threshold, so exactly 3 charges standing with a premier money market balance of exactly 5000.00 reaches the first case, and exactly 2 charges standing reaches the first limb of the second.
